established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) can be used to generate or synthesize network configuration templates and to translate high-level natural-language intent into low-level network configurations in prototype/benchmark systems.
limitations: Evaluations are primarily on prototypes, benchmarks or emulators rather than production deployments
Task scope, dataset size, and vendor/device diversity are limited in reported studies
Reported success varies by task difficulty and prompt/specification quality

established_findings.statement: Constraint-, validator-, or verifier-guided generate→validate→repair workflows measurably improve the correctness or reliability of model-generated artifacts compared to unconstrained generation in reported prototypes.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical + methodological (prototype experiments and surveys on verification/validation)
limitations: Cross-domain evidence includes domains outside networking (e.g., music, SQL) where verifier designs differ
Scale and heterogeneity of network scenarios tested are limited
Improvement magnitude depends on validator fidelity and repair-loop design

established_findings.statement: LLM-driven and agentic systems exhibit recurring failure modes (hallucination, prompt sensitivity, overconfidence/sycophancy, affective misgrounding) that affect operational trustworthiness; mitigation techniques such as secure prompt frameworks and grounding (RAG/validators) are active remedies.
limitations: Failure-mode characterizations span multiple application domains and may differ in operational NetOps contexts
Mitigation effectiveness depends on implementation details and evaluation rigor

unresolved_questions.statement: Whether LLM-generated configurations and intent-translation pipelines are safe, correct, and robust enough for direct deployment across heterogeneous, vendor-diverse production networks remains unresolved.
limitations: Existing studies report prototypes, emulation or limited deployments; none present broad production-scale vendor-diverse validation
Safety and rollback/impact-on-live-traffic evaluations are not comprehensively reported

unresolved_questions.statement: The effectiveness and operational cost (latency, compute, human oversight burden) of verifier-assisted repair loops when scaled to continuous, real-time NetOps workflows is not established.
limitations: Existing evaluations show correctness improvements but do not fully quantify runtime/resource costs or human-in-the-loop requirements at operation scale
Cross-domain verifier evidence may not transfer cleanly to NetOps constraints

unresolved_questions.statement: There is no consensus on standardized benchmarks, metrics, and evaluation protocols that fully capture operational correctness, safety, and rollback behaviors for agentic LLMs in NetOps.
limitations: Several proposals and preliminary frameworks exist, but comprehensive, widely adopted benchmarks and shared datasets are not yet established

candidate_gaps.statement: A gap exists for open, standardized, reproducible NetOps agent benchmarks and emulation-enabled testbeds that combine failure injection, telemetry, and verifiable oracles for configuration correctness and policy compliance.
limitations: Prototypes and frameworks have been published, but no single comprehensive benchmark/testbed has emerged as a standard
Creating full oracles for complex operational correctness (e.g., performance impact, multi-hop safety) is challenging

candidate_gaps.statement: Methodological gaps remain in reproducible LLM-for-NetOps experimentation: preregistration, prompt/version tracking, multi-run sensitivity analyses, and artifact release are unevenly practiced.
limitations: Awareness papers and audits document the issues; adoption of rigorous preregistration and artifact-sharing in NetOps-specific studies is still nascent

candidate_gaps.statement: There is limited cross-disciplinary empirical evidence evaluating bounded/contained agentic architectures (runtime assurance, explicit autonomy boundaries) applied to NetOps with measurable safety guarantees.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: conceptual frameworks + prototype analyses + safety surveys
limitations: Frameworks and architectural proposals exist, but end-to-end empirical validations in operational NetOps settings with quantified safety guarantees are sparse

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven production-ready and safe for fully autonomous, unsupervised deployment across heterogeneous enterprise networks (no supplied record reports broad production deployments or comprehensive production-scale safety validation).

Verifier-assisted repair definitively eliminates hallucination/misconfiguration risk in NetOps (supplied evidence shows improvements in prototypes or other domains but not elimination of risk at production scale).

Published NetOps LLM studies universally follow rigorous preregistration, multi-run sensitivity analysis, and artifact release best practices (evidence shows uneven adoption and explicit prompt-sensitivity/reproducibility concerns).
